prompt: Sawyer's family took a road trip from Washington, DC to Duck, NC. On the way, they stopped for lunch in Richmond, VA, which was 106 miles from DC and 174 miles from Duck, NC. They traveled at an average speed of 58 mph from DC to Richmond, and after lunch it took them 3 hours and 12 minutes to get to Duck. What is Sawyer's family's average speed in miles per hour for the entire trip from Washington, DC to Duck, NC (disregard the time spent at rest stops, lunch, etc.)? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Total distance ÷ total time
solutions.body:
Distance: $106 + 174 = 280$ miles. Time: $\frac{106}{58} \approx 1.8276$ h plus $3.2$ h $= 5.0276$ h. Speed: $280 \div 5.0276 \approx 55.7$ mph.

**Answer: 55.7 mph**

prompt: Sawyer's family took a road trip from Washington, DC to Duck, NC. On the way, they stopped for lunch in Richmond, VA, which was 106 miles from DC and 174 miles from Duck, NC. They traveled at an average speed of 58 mph from DC to Richmond, and after lunch it took them 3 hours and 12 minutes to get to Duck. On the return trip, Sawyer's family decides to stop to take a break in Williamsburg, VA, which is 126 miles from Duck, NC and 153 miles from Washington, DC. If Sawyer's family drove at a speed of 54 mph from Duck to Williamsburg, what must their average speed, in mph, be for the rest of the trip so that their driving time from Duck to DC is the same as their total driving time from DC to Duck (disregard the time spent at rest stops, lunch, etc.)? Express your answer as an integer.

solutions.title: Time remaining
solutions.body:
DC → Duck took $\frac{106}{58} + 3.2 \approx 5.0276$ h. Duck → Williamsburg: $126 \div 54 \approx 2.3333$ h. Time left: $5.0276 - 2.3333 = 2.6943$ h. Speed: $153 \div 2.6943 \approx 56.8 \approx 57$ mph.

**Answer: 57 mph**

solutions.title: Fractions
solutions.body:
Total time $\frac{729}{145}$ h; first leg $\frac{7}{3}$ h. Remaining: $\frac{729}{145} - \frac73 = \frac{2187 - 1015}{435} = \frac{1172}{435}$ h. Speed $= 153 \cdot \frac{435}{1172} \approx 56.79 \approx 57$ mph.

**Answer: 57 mph**

prompt: Sawyer's family took a road trip from Washington, DC to Duck, NC. On the way, they stopped for lunch in Richmond, VA, which was 106 miles from DC and 174 miles from Duck, NC. They traveled at an average speed of 58 mph from DC to Richmond, and after lunch it took them 3 hours and 12 minutes to get to Duck. On the return trip, Sawyer's family stopped to take a break in Williamsburg, VA, which is 126 miles from Duck, NC and 153 miles from Washington, DC. They drove at a speed of 54 mph from Duck to Williamsburg, and planned to drive the rest of the way in exactly the time that would make their driving time from Duck to DC the same as their total driving time from DC to Duck, which requires an average speed of about 57 mph. There was road work between Williamsburg and DC. Sawyer's family had to reduce their speed to 45 mph for 20 miles and to 30 mph for 10 miles. If they were able to maintain 57 mph for the rest of the drive from Williamsburg to DC, how much time was added compared with their planned driving time from Williamsburg to DC (disregard the time spent at rest stops, lunch, etc.)? Express your answer in minutes to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Actual minus planned
solutions.body:
Planned Williamsburg → DC time: total DC → Duck time $\frac{106}{58} + 3.2 \approx 5.0276$ h minus Duck → Williamsburg $126/54 \approx 2.3333$ h $= 2.6943$ h.
Actual: $\frac{20}{45} + \frac{10}{30} + \frac{123}{57} \approx 0.4444 + 0.3333 + 2.1579 = 2.9356$ h.
Added: $2.9356 - 2.6943 = 0.2413$ h $\approx 0.2413 \times 60 \approx 14.5$ minutes.

**Answer: 14.5 minutes**

solutions.title: Work in minutes
solutions.body:
Planned: $2.69425 \times 60 \approx 161.66$ min. Actual: road work $\frac{20}{45} \cdot 60 + \frac{10}{30} \cdot 60 = 26.67 + 20 = 46.67$ min, plus $\frac{123}{57} \cdot 60 \approx 129.47$ min, total $\approx 176.14$ min. Added $\approx 176.14 - 161.66 \approx 14.5$ min.

**Answer: 14.5 minutes**
